title: ThemeRichColor semantic token roles (background/text/border + subtle variants)
answers: Which color token should I use for a solid button background vs an alert background?
What's the difference between background, text, border, subtleBackground and subtleBorder on a theme color?
Why do old tokens like main/shade/transparent still work but shouldn't be used?
body: ThemeRichColor now has a consistent token set used the same way across components: background/backgroundEmphasis = solid-fill normal/hover (buttons, switch active bg); text/textEmphasis = colorful text, text-button text normal/hover; border = strong colorful border (outline button border, focus ring); subtleBackground/subtleBorder = softer surfaces that shouldn't match a solid button (Alert background/border, outline-button hover background). packages/grafana-data/src/themes/createColors.ts:createColors falls back subtleBackground→background and subtleBorder→border when a theme/color doesn't define them, so custom/plugin themes keep rendering unchanged. Tokens main, shade, transparent, transparentBorder, solidBackground, solidBorder are deprecated/no-longer-needed — don't add new usages of them; prefer the tokens above. Schema additions live in packages/grafana-data/src/themes/types.ts:ThemeRichColorInputSchema and must be mirrored in schema.generated.json.
applies: grafana-data theme color definitions and any grafana-ui component consuming theme.colors[severity|variant]
says: Alert notification boxes look too aggressive with solid backgrounds that resemble action buttons.
Outline buttons should display a soft subtle background tint when hovered by users.
The toggle switch active fill color lacks clear visual emphasis on cursor hover.
Make banner notice borders and backgrounds gentler so they do not overpower page content.
Clickable text button labels do not highlight clearly with accent color when hovered.
search: ThemeRichColor semantic tokens use a consistent role set: background/backgroundEmphasis for solid fills, text/textEmphasis for colorful text, border for strong colorful outlines, and subtleBackground/subtleBorder for softer surfaces. The createColors function in packages/grafana-data/src/themes/createColors.ts implements fallback logic (subtleBackground→background, subtleBorder→border) to maintain backward compatibility with custom/plugin themes. Deprecated tokens (main, shade, transparent, transparentBorder, solidBackground, solidBorder) must not be used in new code. Schema additions in packages/grafana-data/src/themes/types.ts:ThemeRichColorInputSchema must be mirrored in schema.generated.json. This guidance applies to all grafana-data theme definitions and grafana-ui components consuming theme.colors[severity|variant].
